question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(2x) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(3x+2) \\ 2x & =3x+2 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=-2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(2x) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{log}⁡(3x+2) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(2(-2)) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{log}⁡(3(-2)+2) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(-4) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{log}⁡(-4)\end{aligned}
$$

However, $\operatorname{log}⁡(-4)$ is not a real number.

Therefore, we conclude that the equation has no real solutions.
